text:
julia_support: Heads-up — multiple customers (ACME + 2) reporting p95/p99 token latency spikes since ~09:10 UTC. They see 202s returned quickly but tokens delayed by ~800-1200ms. Suspect queueing/backpressure on GPU pool.

mike_oncall: Looking now. Any recent deploys or config changes around 09:00?

slo-bot: Deploy: ref=main@a1b2c3 by dan_runtime at 09:02 UTC (status: success)

carol_sre: I pulled metrics: admit_queue_length on gpu-pool-2 jumped at 09:05 -> from ~20 to ~130, CPU on control-plane spiked too. Tail latencies for small requests climbed.

dan_runtime: I rolled a change to default shard max_concurrency yesterday (256 -> 128) to reduce OOMs. Could be tightening admission and pushing requests to queue.

lee_infra: Admission controller logs show repeating warnings:
```
WARN admission: enqueueing request tenant=acme route=/v1/generate size=183
queue_len=127 backlog_ms=900
```

julia_support: Customer repro (ACME):
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.xyz/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"xlarge","prompt":"hi","max_tokens":10}'
```
They see HTTP 202 immediately but tokens stream starts ~800-1200ms later.

mike_oncall: Can someone confirm per-tenant concurrency and fairness rules? Maybe big/batched requests are starving small ones.

carol_sre: Querying queue by tenant -> top queued: acme (34), betaCorp (22), gamma (18). Also correlation between long-running batched jobs and small-request tail.

dan_runtime: That matches the concurrency change theory — fewer concurrent slots means longer-lived requests occupy active slots and smaller fast requests end up in the admit queue. Also KV-cache eviction pattern looks worse; more cold-cache penalty.

lee_infra: Quick mitigation applied: bump per-pod concurrency to 192 on gpu-pool-2 and enable burst_mode=true for 15m to clear backlog. Patching now.

slo-bot: Action: cluster-config change applied to gpu-pool-2 by lee_infra at 09:27 UTC

mike_oncall: Monitor p95/p99 and queue_len. If no improvement, roll back that autoscaler change.

carol_sre: After the bump p95 for small payloads dropped from ~420ms -> ~160ms. p99 improved but still around ~620ms. Queue_len down to ~30.

dan_runtime: For short-term routing: I'll add a rule to preferentially admit requests with payload_tokens <= 32 (priority path) to reduce head-of-line blocking. Will canary 10% of traffic to gpu-pool-2.

julia_support: Please timestamp ETA so I can tell customers.

dan_runtime: Canary started at 09:40 UTC. Early numbers: small-request p99 -> 230ms on canary, queue_len for small reqs nearly zero.

lee_infra: Created follow-up ticket INFRA-1342 to revisit default concurrency and add a regression test for mixed workloads + fairness.

mike_oncall: Owners: dan_runtime (routing patch / canary), lee_infra (cluster config rollback plan + infra ticket), carol_sre (metrics/dashboards + postmortem), julia_support (customer comms). Reconvene 10:00 UTC if anything changes.

julia_support: I'll update ACME and the other impacted customers with the mitigation timeline. Thanks team :thumbsup:

carol_sre: Note for postmortem: consider adding a small-request priority queue or weighted fairness in admission controller to avoid future HL blocking by long-running batched jobs.

mike_oncall: Agreed. Also add a synthetic test in CI that mixes long batch jobs + many tiny requests to catch this in future pre-deploy checks.

julia_support: Closing loop — customers report improvement after 09:45 UTC. Will follow up in the ticket with logs and repro.
